brief:
BRIEF FOR TEAM TS3012, before meeting d. Based on meetings a to c only.

WHAT HAS BEEN DECIDED (CURRENT)
- Speaker A, the Project Manager, set the production cost target at about 12.5 Euros in meeting a. [TS3012a: "The production price, twelve and a half Euros, approximately."]
- Speaker D, the Marketing Expert, reported 75% of users find remotes ugly and 50% use few buttons in meeting b. [TS3012b: "seventy five percent of the users find most remote controls ugly"; TS3012b: "uh fifty percent say they only So that's the most important things"]
- Speaker D, the Marketing Expert, reported teletext relevance is 6.5/10 and over 60% want voice recognition in meetings b and c. [TS3012b: "on the scale of zero to ten they six and a half"; TS3012c: "Um uh more than uh sixty percent"]
- Speaker A, the Project Manager, decided the remote is universal, uses push-buttons, and has a leaner rounded shape in meetings b and c. [TS3012b: "I think it's universal. I think we should go for universal"; TS3012c: "Okay. So push-buttons we will use"]
- Speaker A, the Project Manager, confirmed the remote uses regular batteries, a rubber case, and round buttons in meeting c. [TS3012c: "Uh energy, we choose regular regular batteries"; TS3012c: "The case, it will be the material will be rubber, suppose"]
- Speaker A, the Project Manager, decided to implement beep and flash for remote recovery and keep the teletext button in meetings b and c. [TS3012b: "Well, I don't think we should remove the button, because there are always people who are using it"; TS3012c: "we are going to implement the beep and the flash thing to recover your remote"]

WHAT CHANGED ALONG THE WAY
- Remote locator changed from a simple beep to a combined beep and flash system in meeting c. [TS3012b: "the beep is a very simple thing to imple implement, just make a button on your T_V_"; TS3012c: "we are going to implement the beep and the flash thing to recover your remote"]
- Case material changed from ruling out wood to deciding on rubber in meeting c. [TS3012c: "No, wood i wood's not an option"; TS3012c: "let's just rule out wood for now and continue"]
- Changeable covers changed from being included for fashion to being excluded from the basic design in meeting c. [TS3012c: "one of these interchangeable covers apparently which will make it a more fashionable product"; TS3012c: "that's not something we're working with in the basic design"]

OPEN ACTIONS AND WHO OWNS THEM
- Speaker A, the Project Manager, will investigate changing buttons and covers together or separately. [TS3012b: "Either either change both the buttons and and the cover or just the cover"]
- Speaker B, the User Interface Designer, will present design ideas on paper at the next meeting. [TS3012b: "I'll put some on paper and present them next time"]
- Speaker C, the Industrial Designer, will research costs for rechargeable batteries, docking stations, LCD, and microphone options. [TS3012b: "I'm going to try to find that out"; TS3012b: "Just to do research into both, w what it costs and what it takes for space"]
- Speaker A asked Speakers B and C to work together on the final internal and external design. [TS3012c: "you should work together on the final design, both on internal and external design"]

DISAGREEMENTS STILL OPEN
- Speaker B, the User Interface Designer, and Speaker C, the Industrial Designer, objected that the LCD screen is too expensive for the 25 Euro price point. [TS3012b: "we're not going to be able to sell it for twenty-five then, with an L_C_D_ screen"; TS3012b: "Even if i if we have this lost unit, then we cannot do it for that price"]
- Speaker C, the Industrial Designer, objected that a signal cannot pop up a TV menu and that unconfigured settings cannot be reached. [TS3012b: "Because the television needs to respond to the signal, and if it doesn't know how"; TS3012b: "If it isn't, then we cannot reach it"]
- Speaker B said rechargeable batteries may be too expensive for the whole package. Speaker B said rechargeable batteries plus a docking station may be too expensive. [TS3012b: "But isn't that expensive in the entire package?"; TS3012b: "isn't that too expensive? 'Cause that means that we have to implement rechargeable batteries"]
- Speaker A, the Project Manager, objected that a double-sided remote wastes buttons and that the design looks boring with just a cover change. [TS3012b: "Yeah, but then you're gonna have a lot of wasted buttons"; TS3012b: "it looks boring really to me"]
